title: Prepare your environment
summary: Add friction and make your chosen actions easier.

friction.title: Reduce automatic access
friction.paragraph1: Leaving the phone outside the bedroom, setting time boundaries, or using the system focus mode can add intentional friction.
friction.paragraph2: The point is not to make something impossible, but to add a few seconds between the impulse and the action. Those seconds can create space for a choice to become possible again.
friction.paragraph3: Useful friction is friction you accept. If you work around a setup almost immediately, try a more realistic setting rather than turning it into a reason to feel you failed.
friction.keyPoint1: Aim for a few seconds of delay, not impossibility.
friction.keyPoint2: Choose friction you are willing to keep.
friction.keyPoint3: Adjust friction that you quickly work around.

avoid.title: Avoiding costs less than resisting
avoid.paragraph1: A longitudinal study observed that people who best reached their goals were not those who resisted most, but those who encountered fewer temptations.
avoid.paragraph2: In other words, self-control often plays out upstream: in how the day and the space are organized, more than in the critical moment.
avoid.paragraph3: That can also remove some guilt: needing to rearrange your environment is not an admission of weakness. It is a strategy consistent with these findings.

ifThen.title: “If… then…” plans
ifThen.paragraph1: A meta-analysis covering many studies showed that forming a specific plan—“if this situation occurs, then I will do this action”—improves goal attainment compared with intention alone.
ifThen.paragraph2: Precision matters: the situation must be recognizable and the action immediately doable. “If I am in bed with my phone after 11 p.m., then I put it back on the desk” is more specific than “I will be careful in the evening.”
ifThen.paragraph3: You can start with two or three plans that match your most frequent situations.
ifThen.keyPoint1: Write the triggering situation, not only the goal.
ifThen.keyPoint2: Choose an action you can start immediately.
ifThen.keyPoint3: Start with two or three plans.

moments.title: Prepare vulnerable moments
moments.paragraph1: If tired evenings recur in your observations, preparing a simple routine or charging a device elsewhere can make the desired choice easier.
moments.paragraph2: Prepare for those moments while they are not happening: deciding in advance may take less effort than choosing in the middle of a difficult moment.
moments.paragraph3: If certain accounts or networks often come before difficult moments, you can adjust access without having to remove everything.

alternative.title: Make the alternative visible
alternative.paragraph1: Prepare an accessible replacement action: a book nearby, a short walk, or a task chosen in advance.
alternative.paragraph2: Removing something leaves a gap, and a gap rarely fills itself in the right direction. The alternative should be at least as reachable as what you removed.
alternative.paragraph3: Your environment works best when it supports a specific intention.

limits.title: What a filter does not do
limits.paragraph1: A blocker can complement a plan, but it cannot resolve a difficulty on its own: it acts on access, not on the situation, emotion, or habit that came before.
limits.paragraph2: Tools based on third-party monitoring also raise questions of privacy and trust. StopCorn does not access your browser activity or history, and it does not transmit web-browsing data.
limits.paragraph3: A technical tool works better as support for a plan than as a substitute for one.

reflectionPrompt: What change to your environment could you make today?
